properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 18 at 12:43PM PDT until October 20 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves. Surf of 3 to 6
feet with local sets to 7 feet, primarily for south-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas. Highest waves on south and southwest facing
beaches.

* WHEN...Now through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion may occur across south-facing
beaches.
properties.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 18 at 3:33PM EDT until October 19 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots and seas 5 to 9 ft,
highest across the Straits of Florida.

* WHERE...Straits of Florida, Hawk Channel, Gulf waters
including the Dry Tortugas, and Florida Bay.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
swamped bows at reef tract mooring balls, and dragging anchors.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced boaters, especially those with smaller vessels,
should avoid operating in these conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 18 at 12:31PM PDT until October 20 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf of 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows
may occur across south-facing beaches especially in the Long
Beach area.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 19 at 5:18AM ChST until October 19 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
9 to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Advisory, South and west facing reefs
of Guam and Rota, and south facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan. For
the high risk of rip currents, South and west facing reefs of Guam
and Rota, and south and east facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As Typhoon Champi continues moving away from
the region, surf will continue to gradually diminish. It should
still remain hazardous through the rest of today, however.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
